doc.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Naming the music and what annoys him about critics
summary: He calls it simply music, blames laymen and critics for labels.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Good statement. I’d like to quote you on that. Keep your ears open. Yeah. When you fellows play tonight and tomorrow, if you had a put a name, a style of what it is you do. Would you call it something? Now we were in L.A. and we heard the Classic Jazz Festival. Is that what you would call it? Or wouldn’t you call it anything?
I wouldn’t call it anything. I always like what Eddie Condon says, we call it music. That’s the way I explain it.
Yeah, it’s hard. Because people ask me well Classic Jazz, what does that mean? And is it different from Dixieland and —
And who gave these names to all these different kinds of music you hear? It’s the layman.
Right. I guess we have to ask the critics then.
You know, the critics, that’s another thing.
Well you could, I often thought I could be a critic’s critic.
Right. You could start writing articles about the critics. What is it that annoys you about them?
Well, they couldn’t make a living — if they played an instrument, they couldn’t make a living playing. So they have to —
